hyperedges.evidence: The authoritative README ties recursive discovery, named leaves and aggregates, per-system packages, explicit host composition, and path:. validation into one extension contract.
The Pi workflow is a scout-to-plan-to-test-pin-to-implementation-to-review-to-finalize pipeline with structured handoffs.
Pi implementation assets are co-located and packaged, while environment selection, standalone review tooling, runtime state, and graph output retain distinct ownership boundaries.
The Herdr package is linked declaratively and verified through clean socket state; tuicr uses the official Herdr wrapper for review integration.
Pi separates read-only analysis roles from narrowly scoped implementation and test writers, with graph extraction allowed only its requested JSON artifact.
The module catalog connects independent leaves, compatibility aggregates, explicit hosts, split deploy-rs roles, explicit Sanctum services, and the supported host set.

nodes.label: GitHub check workflow
nodes.content: The check workflow runs on pushes and pull requests, checks out the repository, installs Nix, runs nix flake check, and builds the environment package.

nodes.label: Project memory
nodes.content: Project memory records Herdr socket-protocol verification precautions, Pi ownership boundaries, and the locations of runtime state and graphify output.

nodes.label: Dendritic Nix flake extension skill
nodes.content: The skill explains how to add NixOS features, packages, and explicitly composed hosts in the recursive flake-parts architecture.

nodes.label: Herdr plugin packaging skill
nodes.content: The skill defines how to package an upstream Herdr release together with a Rust plugin, link the plugin declaratively, and verify it with clean runtime state.

nodes.label: Repository agent guidance
nodes.content: Repository guidance describes recursive flake architecture, named module leaves, hosts, package consumers, secrets, and validation commands.

nodes.label: Claude repository guide
nodes.content: The guide documents commands, recursive auto-import, NixOS module boundaries, hosts, wrappers, desktop behavior, Ubuntu support, and Pi integration.

nodes.label: Project notes
nodes.content: Notes describe provider-independent Pi model routing, review and workflow extensions, graphics startup, SkillOpt-Sleep, steerable subagents, Sanctum migration, module boundaries, deploy-rs roles, and co-located Pi implementation.

nodes.label: Root flake README
nodes.content: The root README is the authoritative guide for adding features, packages, and hosts, and describes validation and deployment workflows.

nodes.label: NixOS module README
nodes.content: The NixOS README catalogs independent feature leaves, compatibility aggregates, package overrides, deploy-rs, and Sanctum service composition.

nodes.label: Pi appended system prompt
nodes.content: The appended system prompt requires responses to start with Daniil, forbids unnecessary code comments and AI attribution, establishes shell preferences, and defines skill triggers.

nodes.label: Pi package README
nodes.content: The Pi README describes co-located agents, extensions, prompts, skills, patches, and support packages while keeping global inputs and runtime state outside the directory.

nodes.label: Committer role
nodes.content: The committer role checks repository type at pipeline start and finalizes commits after review, using Jujutsu when .jj exists and enforcing atomic commit quality.

nodes.label: Graphify extractor role
nodes.content: The graphify-extractor role is a bounded semantic extraction worker that reads only supplied files and writes nodes, edges, and hyperedges as JSON to an explicitly requested chunk path.

nodes.label: Escalated implementer role
nodes.content: The escalated implementer retries failed plan items, changes only assigned files, runs pinned tests, and reports structured PASS or FAIL status for each item.

nodes.label: Implementer role
nodes.content: The implementer executes bundled plan items in order, preserves item boundaries, runs pinned tests, and returns structured completion status and changed files.

nodes.label: Output semantics role
nodes.content: The output-analysis role interprets large logs by mapping phases, separating primary failures from noise, building a causal narrative, and proposing next checks.

nodes.label: Planner role
nodes.content: The planner converts scout findings into a concrete checklist, file lists, test expectations, risks, and ordered implementation batches without making code changes.

nodes.label: Reviewer role
nodes.content: The reviewer performs read-only diff review against a plan, checks correctness, security, scope, and test integrity, and emits Critical, Warnings, and Suggestions sections.

nodes.label: Scout role
nodes.content: The scout performs focused read-only reconnaissance, retrieves exact file ranges, identifies key code and dependencies, and hands architecture findings to a planner.

nodes.label: Tester role
nodes.content: The tester pins expected behavior before implementation, opens a Jujutsu commit when applicable, writes a failing regression or correctness test, and reports its target files and change ID.

nodes.label: AI review prompt
nodes.content: The AI review command attaches to exactly one active tuicr session, performs read-only review, and writes actionable comments with the Pi AI reviewer username.

nodes.label: Recursive flake-parts module discovery
nodes.content: Every ordinary .nix file is automatically imported as a flake-parts module; underscore-prefixed files are excluded and require explicit imports.

nodes.label: Independent NixOS feature leaf
nodes.content: A feature leaf is a named, independently usable flake.nixosModules output with explicit prerequisites and an enable option when it changes system behavior.

nodes.label: Compatibility aggregate module
nodes.content: Aggregates such as base, general, desktop, deploy-rs, and sanctum preserve convenient compositions while leaf membership remains explicit.

nodes.label: perSystem package output
nodes.content: Packages are exported under perSystem.packages; self' is used within perSystem, while NixOS modules select self.packages for the host platform.

nodes.label: Explicit host composition
nodes.content: Hosts expose separate configuration and hardware modules, compose them in default.nix, retain a compatibility aggregate, and build configurations through mkHost.

nodes.label: Flake validation workflow
nodes.content: Validation includes alejandra formatting, nix flake check with path:. and show-trace, host closure builds, and optional statix linting.

nodes.label: Push and pull-request CI
nodes.content: GitHub Actions installs Nix and runs flake evaluation plus an environment build for push and pull-request events.

nodes.label: Pi package integration
nodes.content: Pi implementation assets are co-located under packages/pi and exported as pi, pi-subagents, and skillopt-sleep, while environment selection remains in packages/environment.nix.

nodes.label: Provider-portable agent model routing
nodes.content: Agent roles declare complexity tiers rather than provider-specific model IDs; extensions resolve authenticated models and use role complexity as default thinking level.

nodes.label: Pi ship pipeline
nodes.content: The deterministic ship workflow proceeds through scout, plan, test-pin, batched implementation, review, and finalization, passing handoffs in memory.

nodes.label: Jujutsu-aware workflow
nodes.content: When .jj exists, roles use Jujutsu rather than Git, describe or edit item commits, preserve atomic changes, absorb fixes, and verify status and log.

nodes.label: Declarative Herdr plugin bundle
nodes.content: A Herdr bundle combines an upstream Herdr derivation, a separately built Rust plugin root, wrappers, and a launcher that links the plugin before executing Herdr.

nodes.label: Clean Herdr protocol verification
nodes.content: Herdr checks must use a fresh socket path and fresh XDG directories or stop an old server to avoid client/server protocol mismatch.

nodes.label: Tuicr human and AI review
nodes.content: Human diff review uses pinned tuicr and the official Herdr wrapper; AI review adds comments to exactly one active session without modifying repository files.

nodes.label: Graphify chunk JSON output
nodes.content: Graphify extraction is constrained to supplied source files and has an explicit exception allowing a machine-readable absolute chunk output path.

nodes.label: Read-only analysis role boundary
nodes.content: Scout, planner, reviewer, output semantics, and AI review roles inspect or analyze without changing repository source files; implementation and tester roles have narrowly assigned write scopes.

nodes.label: Structured agent handoff
nodes.content: Pi roles use mechanically parsed headings and structured status sections to transfer plans, tests, implementation outcomes, and review findings.

nodes.label: Wrapper-based application configuration
nodes.content: Application configuration is implemented with Nix wrapper libraries rather than home-manager, with aggregate packages supplying the standard environment and desktop session.

nodes.label: Explicit Sanctum service membership
nodes.content: Sanctum service leaves import shared core and are explicitly listed in the sanctum aggregate; adding a module cannot silently enable a production service.

nodes.label: Independent deploy-rs roles
nodes.content: Deploy-rs is split into server and initiator features; the initiator installs the client, while activation and passwordless privileges are separately controlled.

nodes.label: Supported NixOS hosts
nodes.content: The flake defines aku, gru, lich, and tai-lung hosts using the explicit configuration/hardware composition pattern.

nodes.label: Environment package
nodes.content: The wrapped environment package bundles the CLI tools and is used as the login shell on NixOS hosts; CI builds it as a smoke check.
